children: The Kobeissi Letter argued Friday that the $6T market cap erasure across U.S. equities over the last 45 days reflects a normal tech
correction driven by extreme, polarized sentiment rather than the popping of an artificial intelligence
bubble.
Since the S&P 500

hit its record high on Oct. 6, U.S. stocks have lost an average of $225B per day over 31 straight trading sessions, Kobeissi noted in an article posted on X. The 45-day stretch has absorbed Iran War headlines, Q3 earnings anxiety, concerns over AI capital expenditures and free cash flow, the October Fed meeting, the midterm elections, and the Nvidia
controversy.
Compounding the stress, Anthropic's
record-shattering

raised over $100B—with institutional demand hitting $400B and retail orders at $100B—draining market liquidity. Hedge funds posted their largest six-week net tech outflow in over a decade, while the Wall Street fear gauge
surged more than 100% from its October low.
The selloff started with legitimate fears about Big Tech's AI spending spree. Combined capital expenditures from Amazon
, Alphabet
, Meta
, and Microsoft

rose $36.9B in Q3 to a record $201.9B—up 356% since Q1 2024, with $1.6T deployed over three years, Kobeissi noted. Meanwhile, S&P 500 companies have reported 31.9% year-over-year EPS growth in Q3, the strongest in at least four years, with actual earnings beating estimates for 13 consecutive quarters.
Clarity on return on investment should emerge by Q1/Q2 2027, Kobeissi said.

Political shifts added fuel. The Democrats' midterm sweep effectively ended what Kobeissi calls the "Trump Put"—the market's confidence that President Donald Trump would intervene during volatility. A Nov. 4 congressional call for an AI ban rattled sentiment further. Kobeissi dismisses outright ban fears as geopolitically untenable—tantamount to surrendering the AI race to China
—though higher corporate bond yields and Federal Reserve Chair Warsh's hawkish stance compound near-term pressure.

With valuations collapsing to extremes—Nvidia's forward price-to-earnings multiple has dropped to just 9x—Kobeissi sees significant bearishness already priced in, creating a compelling risk-reward setup for high-quality tech names once liquidity returns—similar to the dip-buying rotation that followed April 2025.

title: Kobeissi isn’t buying the AI bubble crash narrative
